thread.title: Tech Stocks to Fall Another 5%: Gene Munster

title: Tech Stocks to Fall Another 5%: Gene Munster
text:
By Shoshanna Delventhal Updated Oct 12, 2018
This week's sell-off , in which both the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) index and the S&P 500 suffered their worst two-day loss in over eight months, disproportionately weighed on America's red-hot technology stocks. Investors' fears regarding tightening monetary policy, rising trade tensions and broader geopolitical instability, coupled with concerns over more regulation on tech companies dragged the Nasdaq Composite Index into correction territory. Now, one top tech analyst turned venture capitalist sees more pain ahead of tech stocks, highlighting safe play Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) as the group's outlier.
(See also: Putting this Painful Sell-Off into Perspective. ) Apple to Withstand Short-Term Weakness in Large-Cap Tech
In an interview with CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Thursday before market open, Gene Munster, the founder of Loup Ventures, warned investors to brace themselves for more heavy selling in the tech space. He forecast another "step down" of 5% for tech giants including Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ), Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) and Facebook Inc. ( FB ), yet did not provide a concrete timeline.
Munster noted that Apple remains a notable exception, given that the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech titan will benefit from higher average selling prices (ASP) for its devices. That said, the venture capitalist isn't recommending dumping tech for the long-haul.
"I'm still bullish on the sector more broadly for other reasons," he stated. "But the near term psychology has a way of playing itself out in historical patterns."
In July, Munster forecast a "divergence" in large-cap tech stocks over the next six to 12 months, telling investors that the sector as a whole could no longer be considered a safe bet.
The market watcher added that Apple and Google parent company Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) "are probably in the best camp."
Tech stocks are making a major comeback in pre-market trading on Friday. Shares of Netflix and Facebook, which both suffered heavy losses earlier this week, are up nearly 5% and 2.1%, respectively. Meanwhile, Amazon stock is higher 4.1%, compared to a 2.2% jump for Google and a 2.5% spike for Apple.
